title: Types of Simple Machines
ques:
Match the simple machine to its real-world example: **Lever, Inclined Plane, Wheel and Axle**.
1. A wheelchair ramp.
2. A seesaw on the playground.
3. A doorknob.

answer.content:
Here is the match:
1. Wheelchair ramp = **Inclined Plane**
2. Seesaw = **Lever**
3. Doorknob = **Wheel and Axle**

explanation: This exercise helps students identify abstract physics concepts in everyday objects.

title: Mechanical Advantage
ques: Why is it much easier to push a heavy box up a long, gentle ramp than it is to lift it straight up into the air?

answer.content: A ramp (an inclined plane) spreads the work out over a longer distance. Because you are pushing over a longer distance, it requires less force (less strength) at any one time than lifting the box straight up against gravity.

explanation: This introduces the fundamental principle of mechanical advantage.

title: Energy Transfer
ques: When you use a pulley to lift a bucket of water from a well, what is the simple machine changing about the force you use?

answer.content: A simple pulley changes the **direction** of the force. Instead of pulling UP to lift the bucket, you can pull DOWN on the rope, which is easier because you can use your body weight to help you.

explanation: This explains how simple machines manipulate force to make work easier.
